solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very good lake crossed by birds and other fliers

indicators.note: the birds go across, round the outside of, the very good and lake pieces

parts.note: coots are water birds
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A lake scene with birds flying over it, among other airborne creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-pilots fly aircraft alongside the captain, so they are fliers besides the birds of the surface.

clue.text: Blaspheme in the absence of saint or priest

indicators.note: the saint is missing from the swearing word, so its letter is taken out

parts.note: to blaspheme is to curse, to swear profanely

explanation.surface: Someone swearing when no holy figure or clergyman is about to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A curé is a French parish priest; the word is used in English without its accent.

clue.text: Get ready to listen — there can be awful panic with pressure, OK?

indicators.note: an awful state is a mess, so the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A worried message: there may be terrible panic under pressure, is that all right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges PANIC, PRESSURE and OK together; 'with' only joins the pieces of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from animals raising their ears when alert, so it means to start paying close attention.

clue.text: They stand to gain property on a river

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so on gives LEG
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Speculators hoping to profit from a riverside estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link joining property to the river, but it is the cricket term: the leg side, also called the on side, is a half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Legatees are people named to receive legacies in a will, so they stand to inherit property.

clue.text: He has left historic parliament: that's a blow

indicators.note: he has gone away from the parliament, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the Rump was the remnant of the Long Parliament in 1648-53

explanation.surface: News that a man walked out of an ancient assembly, presented as a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rump Parliament is written with its article, THE RUMP; taking out 'He' leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trump is an old word for a trumpet blast, the sound blown on the instrument.

clue.text: Regions suffering setback with introduction of a tyrant

indicators.note: the word a is introduced into the reversed regions
a setback sends the regions word backwards

parts.note: parts of a country are its regions

explanation.surface: Territories suffer a reverse when a despot is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' turns PARTS into STRAP, and A goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, and by extension any petty despot.

clue.text: A slowing down when politician gets in a sort of depression

indicators.note: the politician enters the musical slowing-down word

parts.note: rit, short for ritardando, is the musical direction to slow down
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An economic slowdown coinciding with a politician's election, a kind of slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A slowing down' sounds economic, but here it is the musical direction ritardando; 'gets in' puts the politician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder, a depression in the body's surface.

clue.text: Vast enterprise deviously penetrated by English agents

indicators.note: the English letter gets into the rearranged words
acting deviously means taking a crooked route, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A huge firm infiltrated by English spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviously' rearranges VAST ENTERPRISE, and 'penetrated by' adds an E among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Representatives act on behalf of others, which is what agents do.

clue.text: Criticise attempt to secure tricky sale making amusing remark?

indicators.note: the criticism word holds the rearranged sale inside it

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: tricky suggests something twisted, so the letters of sale are mixed up

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A salesman tries to close a difficult deal by cracking a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges SALE into LEAS; 'to secure' has the criticism word hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light joking comment made in conversation.

clue.text: College fellow keeps All Saints Day, having been raised in a bygone age

indicators.note: the college officer holds the date inside him

parts.note: a dean is a senior fellow of a college

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: All Saints Day falls on 1 November, written 1 NOV with 1 as I

explanation.surface: A don observing a church feast after being brought up in olden times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been raised' turns I NOV upwards into VONI, which DEAN holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devonian is a geological period about 400 million years ago, so the adjective describes something from a very ancient era.

clue.text: Anger about home, awkward, not half — it lets in water

indicators.note: the anger word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: rage is anger
in, as in staying in, means at home

indicators.note: only half of the clumsy word is used

parts.note: gauche means socially awkward

explanation.surface: A furious, clumsy rant about home, ending with a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first half of the word for awkward; 'it lets in water' is a cryptic hint rather than a dictionary definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain gauge is an open container that collects rainfall to measure it, so it is designed to let water in.

clue.text: Fellow with inner power is the symbol of a nation

indicators.note: the power letter is placed inside the fellow word

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a male
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A man of inner strength who embodies his country.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple leaf is Canada's emblem, on its national flag.

clue.text: Flap that's not right for take-off

indicators.note: the right letter is not included, so it is dropped

parts.note: a skirt can be a flap, as on a saddle or a hovercraft

explanation.surface: An aircraft flap that is set wrong for getting airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' sounds like flight, but it means a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch mimicking something, a parody or send-up.

clue.text: In concerts I observe people with legitimate expectations

indicators.note: I and the observing word go in the concerts word

parts.note: the Proms are the BBC's summer series of promenade concerts in London
to see is to observe

explanation.surface: A concertgoer notices people with reasonable hopes in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are an annual BBC season of classical concerts held in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A promisee is someone to whom a promise is made, so they can rightly expect it to be kept.

clue.text: What one of the children, as Spooner would have it, is very dull?

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famed for swapping word starts, signals that the opening sounds are exchanged

parts.note: which is a question word asking what
a daughter is one of a family's children

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which child is the boring one.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of WHICH DAUGHTER gives DITCH WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as dull as ditchwater' makes stagnant drain water the standard of extreme tedium.

clue.text: One is 'Mr Opera' possibly?

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone nicknamed Mr Opera, perhaps the top man of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges I, IS and MR OPERA; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is a manager who stages operas and concerts, just the person to be called Mr Opera.

clue.text: Commends a very quiet hour of prayer

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
Lauds is the dawn office in the church's canonical hours

explanation.surface: Praising a silent time of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud someone is to praise or commend them.

clue.text: Frenchman's material?

definitions.meaning: a common French masculine first name, a Frenchman's name
a strong twilled cotton fabric used for workwear and denims

explanation.definitionFit: The French equivalent of John, and also the cotton twill from which jeans are named.

clue.text: Composer's great achievement sitting on poetic island

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a coup is a notable success
Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A composer's triumph while resting on a lyrical isle.
explanation.definitionFit: François Couperin was a French Baroque composer of harpsichord music.

clue.text: The stick American English gets

indicators.note: the answer gets letters from the two words, taking them from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A cultural comparison: the punishment an American or English pupil receives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is the hiding signal: the letters run across the end of American and the start of English.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane was the rod used for corporal punishment in schools, so 'the stick' names it.

clue.text: Phony communicator offering formula for rubbish joke?

indicators.note: a formula is a recipe, so the answer is read as the instructions that produce the words that follow

parts.note: rubbish is rot and a joke is a cod; rot plus cod is the word doctor spun round

explanation.surface: A dishonest press officer whose recipe produces a lame gag.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue, signalled by 'formula for': 'rubbish joke' is ROT + COD, and spinning DOCTOR round gives ROTCOD. COD is British slang for a hoax or joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a political publicist who puts a misleading slant on the news.

clue.text: Mild person not in religious group, one having been put out

indicators.note: one is expelled from the person, so that letter goes

parts.note: a gentile is someone who is not Jewish
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A mild outsider to a faith, after someone was expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle and mild are synonyms for a kindly, soft temperament.

clue.text: Desolate area with a wild animal crossing street

indicators.note: the animal phrase goes across, round, the street

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A barren place where an antelope wanders across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasteland is barren, uncultivated ground, a bleak and empty region.

clue.text: Daughter: one who should pay widow's share

parts.note: an ower is a person who owes

explanation.surface: A daughter named as the debtor for her widowed mother's portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dower was the part of a dead husband's estate that his widow was entitled to for life.

clue.text: Way line emerges from poet

indicators.note: the line comes out of the poet's name, so it is removed

parts.note: Sylvia Plath was an American poet

explanation.surface: How a line of verse comes out of a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a way or route to follow.

clue.text: St Paul's man having traumatic experience with church lapsing

indicators.note: the church falls away, so its letters are dropped

parts.note: a wrench is a painful parting

explanation.surface: A cathedral figure suffering a trauma as his faith lapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St Paul's man' sounds like the apostle's follower but means the cathedral's architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London.

clue.text: Region's publication

definitions.meaning: an expanse of land, read as region is
a short pamphlet, especially a religious or political one

explanation.definitionFit: A tract is both a stretch of land and a short propaganda pamphlet.

clue.text: Individual conveyed by motorist towards the sea

indicators.note: the motorist carries the individual word inside

parts.note: a driver is a motorist
own means individual, particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A person given a lift by a motorist on the way to the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downriver means following the current to the river's mouth, toward the coast.

clue.text: Plant by river in pattern on the box

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
the aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A flower growing beside a river, within a design on a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A raster is the pattern of scanning lines that builds the image on a television screen.

clue.text: Family member making the sound of a big star

parts.note: grand means big

indicators.note: the end of the answer is said like the word for a star

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A relative whose voice booms like a celebrity's.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is a child's son, a relative two generations down.
